title: 3 Stocks in a Bull Rally Right Now
author: Tracey Ryniec
description: While AI stocks face uncertainty following NVIDIA CEO's resignation, several non-technology companies are breaking out to new highs with strong earnings. Visa beat earnings again with 21.4% YTD gains and raised its dividend 16%. Ralph Lauren reported strong full-price demand and raised FY2027 guidance with 10.3% YTD gains. Eli Lilly surged 23% in one month on 39% revenue growth driven by GLP-1 products Mounjaro and Zepbound, raising full-year earnings guidance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Consistent earnings beats since 2008 IPO, strong payment and cross-border volume growth, 16% dividend increase, 21.4% YTD gains at new all-time highs, and expected 13.2% earnings growth in FY2027 with reasonable forward P/E of 28.

Beat consensus estimates, strong full-price demand across all regions led by Asia, successful US Open collection, raised FY2027 guidance, expected 12.8% earnings growth, and Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating despite being near all-time highs.

Beat consensus estimates, 39% Q3 revenue growth from GLP-1 products (Mounjaro and Zepbound), raised full-year earnings guidance, 23% surge in one month, 46.1% expected earnings growth in 2026, and trillion-dollar market cap status despite elevated forward P/E of 40.

title: Lightspark Launches Agent Accounts for AI Agents to Make and Receive Payments
author: Not Specified
description: Lightspark launched Agent Accounts, enabling AI agents to hold, spend, and transfer money on behalf of individuals and businesses across multiple payment methods and currencies. The platform supports payments via Visa cards and direct transfers between Agent Account holders, with account owners maintaining control through spending limits and approval requirements. The service connects to banks and payment networks in 65 countries.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Visa is mentioned as an existing payment network partner integrated into Lightspark's solution, but the article does not indicate any new strategic partnership or material impact on Visa's business. It is referenced as infrastructure rather than as a primary beneficiary.

title: AXP Expands Its Lounge Network: Can Premium Benefits Pay Off?
author: Na
description: American Express is expanding its Centurion Lounge network with new locations at Newark and Heathrow airports opening in 2027-2028, complementing its existing 33 lounges and access to 1,550+ lounges globally. The strategy supports its Platinum Card refresh, which raised annual fees to $895, with Q3 2026 net card fees growing 16% year-over-year, outpacing 8% billed business growth. However, expansion brings increased construction and operating expenses.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 16% year-over-year growth in net card fees, successful Platinum Card refresh with fee increase gaining traction, expanding lounge network enhancing premium card value proposition, and outperformance against industry decline of 13.9% over six months.

Competitive lounge offering through LoungeKey partnership with 1,600+ lounges, but partnership-based model limits direct infrastructure investment and competitive differentiation compared to AXP's owned lounges.

Offers premium travel benefits through DragonPass partnership with 1,200+ lounges, but similar to Mastercard, relies on partnerships rather than owned infrastructure, providing less direct competitive advantage.

title: Visa and American Express Both Raised Their Dividends 16% This Year, but Only 1 of the Stocks Is Up in 2026
author: Eric Volkman
description: Despite both Visa and American Express raising dividends by 16% this year, their stock performances have diverged significantly. Visa is up 22% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500, while American Express has fallen 14%. The difference stems from American Express missing revenue estimates in consecutive quarters and struggling to control expenses, while Visa benefits from favorable regulatory developments and its asset-light business model.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock up 22% year-to-date, significantly outperforming S&P 500's 8% gain. Benefits from asset-light business model, strong quarterly performance meeting analyst expectations, and favorable regulatory environment with CCCA exempting open-loop operators.

Stock down 14% year-to-date despite 16% dividend raise. Missed revenue estimates in two consecutive quarters, expenses growing faster than revenue (12% vs 10% in Q2), and negatively impacted by interest rate sensitivity as a closed-loop issuer and lack of progress on CCCA legislation.

Stock up 16% year-to-date, outperforming S&P 500. Benefits from similar advantages as Visa as an open-loop operator and raised dividend by nearly 15% in 2025, demonstrating strong financial performance.

title: SoFi Technologies vs. Toast: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
author: Sarah Sidlow
description: The article compares two fintech companies for 2027 investment potential. SoFi Technologies, a digital bank with 17.1 million members, reported 73% net income growth and is expanding into digital asset settlement. Toast, a restaurant software platform serving 170,000+ locations, grew revenue 24.1% with $608 million in free cash flow. Despite Toast's stronger recent performance (140% three-year return vs. SoFi's 130%), the analyst recommends SoFi due to its larger addressable market, product diversification, and potential S&P 500 inclusion.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong member growth (17.1M, up 35%), 73% net income growth, expanding into digital assets, larger addressable market, and analyst recommendation for 2027 despite lower recent performance. Meets S&P 500 eligibility criteria.

Solid three-year returns (140%), strong Q3 results with 8,500 net new locations, 24% ARR growth to $2.5B, $608M free cash flow, and AI-powered service expansion. Lower forward P/E ratio (23.8 vs. 18) suggests better valuation.
Mentioned as a partner for SoFi's stablecoin settlement expansion, indicating strategic collaboration but no direct investment thesis presented.
Mentioned as a competitive threat in the restaurant payment space but no detailed analysis or investment recommendation provided.
